unit.why: A legend about Nahmanides (Ramban), his apostate son, and the Pope, ending with a moral lesson for women on raising children; not about Hasidic figures.

stories.start_quote: דרשה של הרמב״ן ישראל שהמיר אינו מזרע
stories.end_quote: בניו בדרך טובים אז טוב להם לעולם
stories.summary_en: After Nahmanides preaches that an apostate cannot be of true Jewish seed, his own son converts. The Pope challenges him, and his wife then reveals that a nobleman raped her and fathered the son. The bitten-off finger proves her account before the Pope, vindicating the Ramban. The tale closes with a moral on mothers educating their children.
